question: What is the state of the art in NLP and computer vision, and how are text and images (and further modalities) combined in multimodal deep learning architectures?
contributions: Overview of SOTA NLP and CV (ch2) with benchmarks and datasets
Architectures by direction: Image2Text, Text2Image, images supporting LMs, text supporting vision, models for both modalities (ch3)
Further topics: further modalities and a challenge-based taxonomy, structured plus unstructured data, multipurpose models and Pathways, generative art (ch4)
Conclusion on societal and compute costs and an epilogue on Stable Diffusion and video generation

limits: Seminar booklet written by students in about one third of a semester; the epilogue concedes it cannot cover the field exhaustively and that some architectures appeared after the chapters were planned in February 2022.
Almost all numbers are reported from other papers; chapter 3 result tables are images, so the figures cannot be checked from the text.
Source-internal inconsistencies: SimCLR ResNet-50(4x) top-1 85.8 in prose vs 76.5 in table; Strubell CO2 249t vs 284t for the big Transformer (different citations); ViT-H layers given as 32.
Chapter 4.1 proposes the authors' own non-contrastive multimodal latent-prediction framework as 'first of its kind' with no results shown.
Chapter 4.2 concedes that many multimodal-plus-tabular studies lack single-modality baselines, tune many hyperparameters and suffer publication bias; structured data alone usually performs best.
Chapter 4.3 concedes that multipurpose models lack suitable metrics and that comparisons are hard; OFA had no specialist baseline for unseen tasks.
Dated: written before GPT-4, LLaVA-style models and open large VLMs; Stable Diffusion appears only in the epilogue.
practices: Prefer large noisy web-scale image-text data with contrastive pretraining over hand-curated labels, accepting some filtering (Sec 3.4.1).
Wrap class labels in a sentence template such as 'A photo of a {label}.' and ensemble prompts for CLIP zero-shot classification (Sec 3.4.3.1).
Freeze large pretrained unimodal models and train only small connecting modules, with zero-initialised gating, to avoid damaging them (Sec 3.5.3, 3.5.4).
Evaluate few-shot models in a true few-shot manner with a dev set separate from test benchmarks (Sec 3.5.3).
Always benchmark a multimodal model against single-modality models, including structured-data-only baselines (Sec 4.2.5).
Use end-to-end joint fusion rather than separate feature-extraction steps, and orthogonalise deep and linear parts to keep Wide & Deep models identifiable (Sec 4.2.4).
Report FID alongside other metrics because FID gives only a one-dimensional view and ignores the precision/recall trade-off (Sec 3.2.5).
Weigh compute, carbon and access costs of large models before scaling; report them (Ch 5, Sec 4.3.5).

terms.definition: projecting a concatenated multimodal input into one representation space
learning separate representation spaces per modality and coordinating them so a common distance function relates points across modalities
the how of learning coordinated spaces; currently mostly contrastive learning
merging modalities inside the model to learn joint representations
given a datapoint in one modality, return a related datapoint in another, by retrieval or generation
merge at input layer / merge latent representations inside the model, end-to-end / fuse the predictions of per-modality models
student predicts the teacher's latent representation of the full input from a masked view, with L1 or L2 regression and no hard negatives
a generator (artist) makes the picture and a model such as CLIP (critic) judges it against the text
